[Research]{.chip}

### Mapping voting blocs

A model borrowed from population genetics finds voting blocs in election returns: neither left nor right, strikingly spatial, and stable across elections.

## Background

- **Associate Professor**, Department of Mathematics, Bowdoin College (2018 to present); Assistant Professor (2012 to 2018)
- **Senior Statistician**, Wellcome Trust Centre for Human Genetics, University of Oxford (2010 to 2012)
- **Research Associate in Statistical Genetics**, University of Bristol (2008 to 2010)
- **Ph.D., Biomathematics**, University of California, Los Angeles
- **B.A., Mathematics**, Pomona College

As we confront the disaster of increasing authoritarianism and its computational and data-based implementation, I think it is incumbent upon us as quantitative scholars that we challenge ourselves to do the difficult work of re-imagining our disciplines freed from their associations with the surveillance state. The [Just Mathematics Collective](https://www.justmathematicscollective.net/) provides some much needed initiative in that direction.
